{{Quote|The citizenry also charges you Xim, Son of Xer, with the unjustified decimation of countless peoples and worlds, including Vodran, Jurzuu, and Ko Vari.''"''<br />''"''Of Vodran I have no recollection.|Adjudicator [[Rexrax Shool]] and Xim the Despot, in the play ''Evocar''|<ref name="XD4">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek05/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part IV: ''Evocar'')|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref>}}
The '''Vodrans''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Egg/Legends|egg]]-laying [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]] who evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vodran/Legends|Vodran]], in the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]]. The Vodrans were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] beings who stood no taller than a [[Human/Legends|Human]], but who exhibited several physiological differences from that species: [[Color/Legends|monochromatic]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]; hard, [[Leather/Legends|leathery]] skin; underdeveloped facial muscles; and a ring of spikes around the face. While peaceful by nature, Vodrans made strong [[Soldier/Legends|fighters]]. Most Vodrans [[The value of many|considered]] the benefits of the collective before those of the individual, showing almost no individuality; the few freethinking Vodrans were considered pariahs and rogues by their fellows. One example, who lived during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], was the unbalanced Vodran [[Xenon Nnaksta]], who became an [[Officer/Legends|officer]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].

Even before the establishment of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Vodrans were [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]]. The legendary Vodran warrior [[Kl'ieutu Mutela]] signed his whole species into servitude through the [[Treaty of Vontor]], and the Hutts imposed their own culture upon the Vodrans and eradicated the reptilian species' independent civilization. The Vodrans believed that their partnership with the Hutts profited both sides, and as such the reptiles readily sacrificed their own lives in great numbers to preserve the ostentatious lifestyles led by their Hutt overlords, even though such wastrel-like activities were one aspect of Hutt culture that the Vodrans did not emulate.

The Hutts initially recruited the Vodrans&mdash;along with the neighboring [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] and [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] species&mdash;to fight the forces of the Human [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] the Despot at the [[Third Battle of Vontor]]. After their success at [[Vontor]], the three species were kept on retainer by the Hutts, commonly for use as enforcers or thugs. The Vodrans proved to be the most loyal slave species in the Hutts' retinue, and they never attempted any rebellion against their masters.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Xenon_Nnaksta_AJ6.jpg|thumb|left|upright|The Vodran face featured spiky horns and black eyes.]]
The Vodrans were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] who came from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vodran/Legends|Vodran]]. They were [[Limb/Legends|two-legged]], [[Blood/Legends|warm-blooded]] [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]],<ref name="ES">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in shape,<ref name="CENC">{{CSWECite|III|310|Vodran (planet)}}</ref> with five-fingered hands that featured thick nails. Their bodies were covered with [[Leather/Legends|leathery]] skin that varied in [[Color/Legends|color]] from olive green to brown.<ref name="GG" /> The skin was hard enough to offer some protection from physical damage.<ref name="UA" />

The Vodran face featured a flat [[Nose/Legends|nose]] and two black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="UA" /> Hard skin combined with underdeveloped muscles to restrict the range of emotions a Vodran could transmit through facial expressions. The face was ringed by horny protuberances that created a ridge of horns about the temples and on the chin.<ref name="GG" />

Vodrans were [[Egg/Legends|oviparous]], with [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] from [[egg clutch]]es; a typical clutch produced two or three children.<ref name="GG" /> Vodrans began their adolescence at twelve [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of age and reached maturity at age seventeen. The average height of an adult was 1.75 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="UA" /> to 1.80 meters, a size that afforded the beings with long legs that allowed them to run as fast as [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="GG" /> At forty-five, age began to take its toll on a Vodran and, at sixty-five, a Vodran was considered old. The average Vodran lifespan was eighty years; any Vodran who lived beyond that age was considered venerable.<ref name="UA" />

The Vodrans were a nimble, sturdy people with acute senses.<ref name="GG" /> Some of them had the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|capacity]] to become users of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="UA" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Vodran.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Vodrans used survival skills to endure the rough environs of their homeworld.]]
{{Quote|The problem with your people is that you think the Hutts are gods.'''"''<br />''"''And by 'your people,' you mean&hellip;''"''<br />''"''Klatooinians, Vodrans, all the various breeds of Niktos. All you faithful species that have sworn fealty to the Hutts.|[[Hedu]] of the Rodian [[Bomu Clan]] and the Klatoonian [[Koax]]|<ref name="Scourge">[[Scourge (novel)|''Scourge'']]</ref>}}
Vodrans had little sense of self and thus showed little individual personality. They instead believed in "[[the value of many]]," seeing the whole species as a group. The physiological restrictions on their facial movements prompted them to convey wishes and emotions with only body language and vocal inflection.<ref name="GG" /> As they thought of the collective before themselves, they had trouble with advanced social conventions such as innuendo and etiquette.<ref name="UA" />

Although the Vodrans established an independent culture based on [[City/Legends|settlements]] made up of huts and inhabited by [[Dianoga/Legends|dianoga]] [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] and [[spinefish]] [[Fishing/Legends|fishers]],<ref name="GG" /> after contact with an outside species, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], the Vodrans served the [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]<ref name="CENC" /> for [[Time/Legends|millennia]] with unswerving loyalty,<ref name="UA" /> a devotion that made them the most dedicated of the Hutts' servant species. While exceptions existed, the great majority of Vodrans were absolutely loyal to Hutt institutions, mostly represented as the [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidics]]&mdash;Hutt families that were in charge of criminal activities. Vodrans eschewed manifestations of individuality in their species, and they prioritized the well-being of their Hutt masters, no matter how many Vodrans had to [[Death/Legends|die]] to protect their superiors' way of life.<ref name="GG" /> Hutts who settled on the planet Vodran exploited their hard-working reptilian servants to keep up opulent activities.<ref name="UA" /> Vodrans believed that their association with the Hutts had been fruitful for their people, and the individual who made it possible, the [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] [[Kl'ieutu Mutela]], was revered by his species.<ref name="GG" />

The Vodrans developed their own culture before making contact with the Hutts. However, as soon as the Hutts began to deal with Vodrans, the master species imposed their own culture and replaced indigenous folkways. A new mythology was created that suggested the Vodrans had only existed from the moment they began their service to the Hutts. While this was historically untrue, Vodrans who lived afterward believed it wholeheartedly, and the Vodrans' civilization, history, and art adapted to reflect that.<ref name="GG" /> The Hutts replaced the ancient [[Vodran language|language of the Vodrans]] with the Hutt [[Language/Legends|tongue]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], although from the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] onward, many Vodrans also learned to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. The Hutts provided the Vodrans with advanced technology, including [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]], but most Vodrans did not dare travel away from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] without the blessing of their Hutt masters.<ref name="UA" /> Nevertheless, many Vodrans had a hard time mastering technology or scientific knowledge.<ref name="GG" />

Like their Hutt overlords, Vodrans organized themselves into [[miniature kajidic]]s, or Vodran clans. Each clan answered to a Hutt kajidic,<ref name="UA" /> and ultimately to the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Clan of Ancients]], which ruled over the Hutt species and its subordinates.<ref name="GG" /> However, one aspect of Hutt culture the Vodrans did not adopt was the Hutt fondness for lounging and leisure. Also unlike Hutts, Vodrans had two-part names, with examples including the names Meido Lycri, Kl'ietu Mutela, Lakren Plooru, and Saran Vydek.<ref name="UA" />

Vodrans had a deep-rooted respect for authority figures, whether Hutt or otherwise. Individual Vodrans rarely tried to obtain personal power. They instead tried to serve Vodran social institutions and, through them, what they considered the greater good. Vodrans valued commitment and consensus, and they expected an individual to accept the ruling of the group, whether it be a Hutt kajidic, a state, a clan, or a union.<ref name="GG" /> A marginal minority of Vodrans showed enough individuality to<ref name="UA" /> reject their society and its principles, overcoming social conditioning and innate tendencies to obey authority. Such people tended to be loners<ref name="GG" /> and escaped from their Hutt masters. Other Vodrans considered such freethinkers to be pariahs, outcasts, and maniacs. While some Hutts cared little about losing the rogue servants, others turned to [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] to track down such fugitives.<ref name="UA" />

In general, Vodrans were naïve,<ref name="UA" /> peaceful, and straightforward. However, they commonly served as enforcers after developing combat skills that drew upon their aggressive potential.<ref name="GG" /> Other commonly learned skills that aided survival in wild, hostile environments because most Vodrans grew up on Vodran, where they faced the threat of huge [[Diet/Legends|predators]] that roamed the steamy jungles and swamps. A mild [[psychosis]] affected some Vodrans and made them fearless daredevils.<ref name="AJ6">{{JournalCite|6|The Greel Wood Haven}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|In fact, just about anyone who had regular dealings with the Hutts has lost credibility&mdash;the Rodians&mdash;except for the Jungle Clans&mdash;Whiphids, Klatoonians, Weequays, Vodrans, Iotrans, Nikto&hellip;|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], on the results of the Hutts' double dealings during the Yuuzhan Vong War|<ref name="UF" />}}
The planet Vodran, full of steamy<ref name="MT">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> jungles and swamps,<ref name="GG" /> was also rich in [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]]<ref name="UA" /> and huge predators. Local species had to evolve quickly to avoid extinction in such a hostile environment. While the dianoga learned to change color<ref name="GG" /> and scavenge,<ref name="MT" /> a species of [[Insect/Legends|insect]]-eating reptiles that lived in the colossal [[Tree/Legends|trees]] instead developed intelligence as a survival tool; these primitive Vodrans learned to hunt and work together and to build settlements in the treetops. They managed to thrive in conditions that would have killed many other species. The Vodrans developed a society of fishers and dianoga hunters who used hanging trees to capture dianoga and spinefish from thatched huts over [[Water/Legends|rivers]].<ref name="GG" />

===Xim Wars===
[[File:Ximsbigrobotguy.png|thumb|left|upright|Xim's war-robots were no match for the Vodrans and their allies.]]
Around [[25,100 BBY]],<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Fire/Legends|fire]] rained down from the skies of the planet Vodran, and entire huts were wiped out. Unable to counterattack, the Vodrans started rebuilding their settlements as they had been.<ref name="XD1">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref> Little did they know that their world had become a battleground in a [[Xim Wars|war]] between the forces of the Hutts and those of a Human [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] named [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] the Despot, who were fighting over control of the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]] in which Vodran was located.<ref name="EA" />

As the Vodrans rebuilt, emissaries approached them. Led by [[Dojundo]] the Hutt,<ref name="XD1" /> the visitors used an old [[language convertor lexicon]] to communicate.<ref name="GG" /> They told of their master, a warrior called [[Kossak Inijic Ar'durv|Kossak]] the Hutt.<ref name="XD1" /> The strangers from afar tried to convince the Vodrans to join Kossak's [[Army/Legends|armies]].<ref name="GG" /> The superstitious Vodrans, in awe of the flaming, flying vehicles and advanced technology of the outsiders, viewed the Hutts as demi-[[Deity/Legends|gods]],<ref name="XD1" /> god-like [[Demon/Legends|demons]],<ref name="GG" /> or even terrible deities.<ref name="UA" /> In fear, they bowed to the offworlders' will<ref name="GG" /> and swore to fight against the enemies of the Hutts in exchange for the secrets of the Hutts' "[[Star/Legends|star]]-[[Magic/Legends|magic]]."<ref name="XD1" />

Kossak's other envoys recruited the [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinians]] from [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]] and the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] from [[Kintan/Legends|Kintan]].<ref name="GATORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> Before the forces could join the war,<ref name="EC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the Hutts forged the [[Treaty of Vontor]], a contract binding the three species of the Si'Klaata [[Star cluster/Legends|Cluster]] in eternal servitude,<ref name="NG">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> as permanently indentured servants,<ref name="UA" /> to the Hutts. The greatest Vodran warrior, Kl'ieutu Mutela, signed for his species. Xim, unaware of the Hutts' new allies,<ref name="GG" /> prepared his janissaries and his new legions of<ref name="HX5">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> of reportedly invincible [[Laser/Legends|laser]]-resistant [[war-robot]]s. Xim intended to deploy all of his forces on Vontor for a last battle, hoping to overwhelm and defeat the Hutts once and for all.<ref name="ED">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

Kossak gathered his [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] at Vontor and Xim sent his [[Trooper/Legends|troops]] to the surface in massive [[Landing barge/Legends|landing barges]]. He did not expect to find one million Klatooinian, Nikto, and Vodran<ref name="GG" /> berserkers<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> waiting for them on the surface,<ref name="GG" /> along with a number of [[Weequay/Legends|Weequays]], another species affiliated with the Hutts. While Xim was sending his [[Warship/Legends|warships]] against Kossak's forces,<ref name="HX5" /> the Vodrans and their new companions destroyed most of Xim's war-robots<ref name="CENC Xim">{{CSWECite|III|342|Xim}}</ref> and then wrecked Xim's [[Orbital platform/Legends|orbital platforms]]<ref name="ED" /> by bombing them. Xim's fleet was destroyed<ref name="HX5" /> in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] except for a few ships that escaped<ref name="GG" /> with the last war-robots.<ref name="ED" />

The Klatooinian [[skald]] [[Pupaku]] wrote a [[The Third Battle|memorial]] of the battle. He provided an elegy for the warriors of the Si'Klaata Cluster, including those he characterized as Klatooinian, Nikto, Vodran, and Weequay brothers-in-arms. According to Pupaku, the warriors resorted to a [[Spice/Legends|spice]]-induced berserker rage to refrain from withdrawing when their robot nemeses approached. The warriors then took the robots to the underground of Vontor to dismantle them, one by one, even as the warriors themselves were killed. The soldiers' sacrifice turned the tide of the battle, the skald claimed: Xim's organic high-ranking [[Officer/Legends|officers]] understood that Xim could be defeated, and they mutinied. Nevertheless, in further generations, [[Historian/Legends|historians]] were unable to confirm Pupaku's claims.<ref name="XD1" />

The [[Third Battle of Vontor]] resulted in Xim's final defeat to the Hutts,<ref name="GG" /> and the Klatooinian, Nikto, and Vodran army proved themselves essential to that outcome.<ref name="CENC Xim" /> The Vodrans came to perceive the battle as a holy war that involved weird beings, new weapons, and magical items that were awarded to them.<ref name="GG" />

===After Xim===
[[File:VodranPlanet.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Vodran, the homeworld of Vodran species]]
Once Xim was defeated, the Hutts added the planet Vodran,<ref name="UA" /> along with the whole of the Si'Klaata Cluster,<ref name="SSR">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> to their empire,<ref name="UA" /> which eventually came to be known as [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="EA" /> The Vodrans started serving their new Hutt masters loyally, and the Hutts used the Vodrans, along with other indentured species, as enforcers, [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], and lackeys to keep control over their domains. The Hutts eradicated Vodran culture and replaced it with beliefs more productive to the conquering species&mdash;including the false idea that the Vodrans existed only from the very moment they started serving the Hutts. Eventually, Hutt [[Realspace/Legends|Space]] came into contact with a wider power, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]; the Hutts then used the Vodrans and their other slaves to build a criminal empire for themselves within the borders of the Republic. As far as the Vodrans were concerned, they regarded their association with the Hutts highly, and they started revering their hero Mutela for signing the Treaty of Vontor.<ref name="GG" />

Circa [[671 BBY]], the thirteen-act theatrical play [[Evocar (play)|''Evocar'']], written by [[Direus'pei]] the Hutt, was posthumously published by his Nikto scribe, [[Ro Vacca]]. The work presented Xim as a sympathetic character who prompted slaves to rebel against their Hutt masters. In the third act, Xim was charged with the murders of people of several worlds, including the planet Vodran, but Xim replied then that he did not recall that world at all. While the Hutts tried to restrict access to ''Evocar,'' it inspired several species, including the [[Evocii]], Klatooinians, and Nikto, to rebel against them. The Vodrans, however, spurned the play and staged no major insurrections.<ref name="XD4" />

Through the years, Hutt inter-clan rivalries exploded commonly as brush-fire wars among the species serving the Hutts, including the Vodrans.<ref name="SOTESB">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> Around the first years of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], a violent urban uprising known as the [[Thruncan Insurrection]] destroyed several of Vodran's cities soon before the start of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="AJ6" />

During the time of the Galactic Empire, Vodrans were officially recognized as sentient beings,<ref name="ES" /> and thus gained the legal right to own and manage corporations.<ref name="AJ6" /> Later, after the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] started military activities against the Empire, the renegade [[Iyra]] [[sentientologist]] [[Tem Eliss]] traveled to Hutt Space to study the species indentured to the Hutts, including the Vodrans, to prove his hypothesis about millennia of genetic and cultural eugenics.<ref name="G6">{{GamerCite|6|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Nikto}}</ref>

The Galactic Empire made an attempt to seize the planet Vodran and rule its native species, but the Vodrans opposed the takeover. As a consequence, much of the Vodran population was [[Speciecide|slaughtered]], with only a small percentage surviving. When the anti-Imperial [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] was created in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], most Vodrans offered their support to it, although they clearly stated that the Vodrans' first allegiance was to the Hutts.<ref name="ES" />

A later conflict known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] prompted the Hutts to attempt to outsmart the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] species and play both sides of the war. The discovery of the Hutts' double-dealings damaged their reputation. Once the war was over, species associated with them, such as the Vodrans, lost prestige and credibility in the greater [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="UF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>

==Vodrans in the galaxy==
[[File:Twilight_Class_expedition.png|thumb|left|Xenon Nnaksta was an individualist Vodran who joined the Rebel Alliance.]]
Vodrans commonly dealt with the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] only through the Hutts: Vodrans rarely traveled without the authorization of their masters. Other species tended to see Vodrans as enforcers and thugs who inevitably represented the interests of the Hutts.<ref name="GG" /> Such a belief was not unfounded; for instance, in [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]],<ref name="tales">[[Tales of the Jedi 3|''Tales of the Jedi'' 3]]</ref> Vodrans served alongside Klatoonians, Nikto, and Weequays, as boarding [[Troop/Legends|troops]] and crew hands for the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Bogga]] the Hutt. [[Grimorg]], Bogga's Weequay chief enforcer, had the job of controlling them.<ref name="EV">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> Accordingly, some enemies of the Hutts targeted Vodrans as part of larger schemes to harass the reptiloids' masters. For example, the Nikto [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Ga'p'tashi]] attacked Vodran-run vessels for such reasons during regime of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="P&P">''[[Pirates & Privateers]]''</ref>

Although Vodrans were rarely seen beyond the borders of Hutt Space,<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> Hutts sometimes sold Vodran slaves to other criminals.<ref name="GG" /> Such transfers represented the only real opportunity for a Vodran to leave Hutt Space.<ref name="UA" /> Indeed, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Daiman]] employed Vodran soldiers to help defend his territory, which was known as the [[Daimanate]]. During a [[Battle of Gazzari|battle]] on the planet [[Gazzari]], a [[Unidentified Vodran soldier|Vodran soldier]] aided in Daiman's defenses against a rival territory known as the [[Odionate]] and a female Human [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] named [[Kerra Holt]]. After being injured and maimed in the fighting, the Vodran was killed by Holt's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].<ref name="KE">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']]</ref> The planet Vodran had no exports, although a native creature known as the dianoga spread throughout the galaxy as [[Larva/Legends|larvae]] for millennia, to the Vodrans' chagrin.<ref name="GG" />

The infamous<ref name="GG" /> and individualistic Vodran [[Xenon Nnaksta]], born in the [[Kudor province]] of Vodran,<ref name="AJ6" /> rejected his species' traditions and became<ref name="GG" /> first the manager and owner of the [[Greel Wood Logging Corporation]], then a survival expert, and lastly a member of the Alliance to Restore the Republic.<ref name="AJ6" /> Promoted to [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]], Nnaksta joined the undercover [[Eclipse Team]] and<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> was still an officer during the days of the New Republic.<ref name="AJ4">{{JournalCite|4|Wanted by Cracken (Star Wars Adventure Journal)}}</ref> Nnaksta was also a victim of a slight dementia, particularly noticeable because he drove recklessly and because he used a [[vibrosaw]] intended to fell trees as his weapon of choice.<ref name="AJ6" />

==Behind the scenes==
The planet Vodran has been part of ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] since the [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] guide ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'' was published in [[1989]] by [[West End Games]] for its ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="MT" /> "[[The Greel Wood Haven]]," an article written by [[Craig Robert Carey|C. Robert Carey]] and published in [[May]] [[1995]] as part of [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 6|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 6]], introduced the Vodran species in relation to that world. The book establishes that a character from an earlier article, Xenon Nnaksta,<ref name="AJ4" /> was a Vodran from the planet Vodran. An illustration by [[David Day]] in the article marks the earliest illustration of the species.<ref name="AJ6" /> Another publication from the same year, ''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'', provides a full description of the Vodrans written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], as well as an image of them by [[Mike Vilardi]].<ref name="GG" />

Since their debut, the Vodrans have featured primarily in roleplaying material&mdash;the one major exception being [[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']], a novel by [[John Jackson Miller]] published in [[2011]].<ref name="KE" /> The roleplaying book ''Galaxy Guide 12'' includes game rules for the species: Vodrans loyal to the Hutts receive a bonus to their willpower to resist betrayal of their masters, so players may role-play loyal Vodrans who enjoy the bonus or outcast Vodrans who do not.<ref name="GG" /> A later role-playing guide written for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' and published in [[2003]], ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', adapts this rule: loyal Vodrans receive a loyalty bonus whenever someone attempts to blackmail or seduce them, but non-loyal ones instead get a bonus to their intelligence abilities.<ref name="UA" /> The two books disagree on the height of an adult Vodran: ''Galaxy Guide 12'' and ''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'' make the average Vodran 1.80 meters tall,<ref name="GG" /> while ''Anthology'' reduces the number to 1.75 meters.<ref name="UA" /> The roleplaying supplement ''[[Pirates & Privateers]]'', published in [[1997]], misspells the species' name ''Vodron''.<ref name="P&P" />

''Galaxy Guide 12'' says that the Hutts made the Vodrans sign themselves into eternal servitude ''after'' their victory in the Third Battle of Vontor.<ref name="GG" /> However, the timeline in [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], published in [[2001]], mentions the treaty being signed before the Hutts defeated Xim.<ref name="ES" /> [[1999]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]'' says that the Hutts and the Vodrans "made a pact" before the battle&mdash;although the treaty is not mentioned by name.<ref name="ED" /> [[2005]]'s ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' says that "two more battles followed [the [[Second Battle of Vontor|Second]] and Third Battles of Vontor], but by that point, the Hutts had forged the Treaty of Vontor." It does not specify whether the treaty was signed before or after the battle.<ref name="EC" /> The [[2010]] novel ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]'' by [[Christie Golden]] details the [[44 ABY]] attack on the [[Fountain of Ancients]] on the planet [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]] that nullifies the Treaty of Vontor for at least the Klatooinians and the Nikto. However, the source makes no mention of the Vodrans, so it is unclear whether the treaty remains in place for them after the attack.<ref name="Al">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref>
